The above captioned criminal revision petitions arise from the order dated 23.04.2014 passed in Special CBI C.C. No.24/2013 by the Court of III Additional District and Sessions Special Judge,
Dharwad wherein the application filed by accused Nos.1, 5 to 7 under Section 227 of Cr.P.C. with a prayer to discharge them was rejected.

Additional District and Sessions Special Judge,
Dharwad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

3. The petitioners herein are arrayed as accused Nos.1 and 5 to 7 in Special CBI C.C. No.24/2013 pending before the Court of III Additional District and Sessions Special Judge, Dharwad, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 120B r/w 420, 467, 468, 471 and 511 of IPC and Sections 7, 13(1)(D) of Prevention of Corruption Act.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the said proceedings, the petitioners herein had filed an application under Section 227 of Cr.P.C. with a prayer to discharge them.

They had raised NC:
2024:KHC-D:1041 C/W CRL.RP No. 100198 of 2014, CRL.RP No. 100215 of 2014, CRL.RP No.
100228 of 2014 various contentions before the Trial Court in support of the prayer made by them in the application seeking discharge.
4. The prayer made in the application was opposed by the learned Special Public Prosecutor by filing statement of objection.
5. The Trial Court after hearing both the sides, vide impugned order dated 23.04.2014, dismissed the application filed under Section 227 of Cr.P.C. by the petitioners herein.
Therefore, they are before this Court.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners have raised various contentions in support of the prayer made in the application filed under Section 227 of Cr.P.C.
The trial Court though has taken note of all the contentions urged on behalf of the petitioners, has failed to consider the same and pass a reasoned order.

They submit that absolutely no reason has been assigned by the trial Court for dismissing the application filed under NC: 2024:KHC-D:1041 C/W CRL.RP No.
100198 of 2014, CRL.RP No. 100215 of 2014, CRL.RP No. 100228 of 2014 Section 227 of Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, they pray to allow the petition.
7. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent has opposed the petition.
He submits that there is no merit in the contentions urged by the petitioners.
There is sufficient material in the charge sheet to prove the charges against the petitioners.
Therefore, the trial Court is justified in dismissing the application.
Accordingly, prays to dismiss the petition.

8. From perusal of the order impugned in this revision petition, it is seen that the trial Court has taken note of the various contention urged by the petitioner's in support of their prayer made in the application seeking discharge.
However, absolutely no reasoning is assigned by the Trial Court for dismissing the application seeking discharge filed by the petitioners.

None of the contentions urged G R Lawhale S/O R P Lawhale vs Central Bureau Of Investigation on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26677082/
5 by the petitioners in support of their prayer has been answered by the trial Court.

entities.text: G R Lawhale S/O R P Lawhale vs Central Bureau Of Investigation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Trial Court has proceeded to dismiss the application on the ground that NC: 2024:KHC-D:1041 C/W CRL.RP No.
100198 of 2014, CRL.RP No. 100215 of 2014, CRL.RP No. 100228 of 2014 CBI police have filed final report and therefore trial is required with liberty to take the defence available under law.
Except the same, there is no other reasoning assigned by the trial Court for rejecting the application filed by the petitioners.

At the stage of considering the discharge application, learned Judge is required to apply his judicial mind to the facts of the case in order to determine whether a case for trial has been made out by the prosecution.
The trial Judge is required to consider whether the charge sheet material produced by the prosecution prima facie discloses the case against accused persons.
9. In the case on hand, no such exercise has been done by the trial Judge while dismissing the application filed by the petitioners seeking discharge.

Learned judge has not answered any one of the contentions urged in support of the prayer made by the petitioners, nor has he referred to any one of the charge sheet material collected by the prosecution which ex-facie disclose that there are NC: 2024:KHC-D:1041 C/W CRL.RP No. 100198 of 2014, CRL.RP No. 100215 of 2014, CRL.RP No.
100228 of 2014 suspicious circumstances against accused.
The order passed on application seeking discharge should be a reasoned order, since the Court decides the precious right of the accused.
In the case on hand, absolutely no reasoning has been assigned by the trial Court for dismissing the application filed by the petitioners seeking discharge.
Therefore the impugned order cannot be sustained in the eye of law.

Considering the fact that proceedings are pending before the trial Court for a considerable period of time, I am of the opinion that the trial Court is required to be directed to consider the application and dispose of the same on merits within a time frame.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER Criminal Revision Petitions are allowed.

The order dated 23.04.2014 passed in Special CBI C.C. No.24/2013 by the Court of III Additional District and Sessions Special Judge, Dharwad dismissing the application filed by the petitioners under Section 227 of Cr.P.C. is set aside.

Registry is directed to forthwith return the records of the trial Court.
